name: Egalin's Grimoire
summary: In the Undercity, Egalin's Grimoire holds the rites for summoning and commanding a voidwalker. A master warlock wrote it as a teaching text for the Temple of the Damned.

sections.title: A Master's Work
sections.body: Egalin's Grimoire records how to call a being of chaos from the Nether. Egalin was a master summoner, renowned for his effortless command of voidwalkers. He passed that skill to his students, including Carendin Halgar. Without the formulas and channeling methods in the book, an unprepared summoner risks being torn apart by the being they call forth.

sections.title: The Scarlet Theft
sections.body: A Scarlet Crusade operative named Perrine stole the grimoire from the Forsaken warlocks and hid it in a chest in a tower in western Tirisfal Glades. The Crusade hated dark magic, yet Perrine seemed to know little of the book's true significance. The tome was treated as seized heretical salvage until Forsaken initiates seeking to master the void retrieved it.

faq.answer: Egalin was a talented warlock who mentored Carendin Halgar. He was the first among them to summon a voidwalker and commanded chaotic entities with ease.

faq.q: Why is Egalin's Grimoire so dangerous?
faq.answer: Egalin's Grimoire contains the incantations and channeling methods for summoning a voidwalker. A warlock who attempts the ritual without mastering these instructions risks being torn apart by the summoned void entity.

faq.q: How did the Scarlet Crusade get the book?
faq.answer: A Scarlet Crusade agent named Perrine stole the tome from the Forsaken warlocks. He hid it in a chest at a Crusade watchtower in western Tirisfal Glades, seemingly unaware of its true magical worth.
Carendin Halgar, the warlock trainer in the Temple of the Damned beneath the Undercity, needs the grimoire to teach new initiates to summon and bind voidwalkers.

angles.text: As a warlock, you can use Egalin's Grimoire to learn the techniques for summoning a voidwalker from the Nether and binding it to your will, a rite of passage for practitioners.
As an undead, recovering the book keeps the Scarlet Crusade from holding a powerful magical artifact stolen from the Undercity's practitioners.
